title: Education on Ballot Secrecy in Schools
what_it_is: Education on Ballot Secrecy in Schools

sections.label: Elections in school curriculum
sections.summary: Social Studies, History and CCE teach elections progressively, but limited curriculum time means ballot secrecy is not included.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Through the Social Studies, History and Character and Citizenship Education 	(CCE) curriculum, students learn how elections allow citizens' interests to be represented and how this contributes to good governance.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The curriculum develops an understanding of the significance of elections progressively.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: At the primary and lower secondary levels, students are introduced to how elections shape our history from self-government to Independence.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: At the upper secondary levels, students learn about how representatives to Parliament are chosen by the people through General Elections.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Students also engage in discussions about the roles of Members of Parliament and the Elected President.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: However, limited curriculum time requires careful selection of content for a strong understanding of citizenship and elections at each stage of the student's development.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Thus, specific topics such as ballot secrecy are not included in the curriculum.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: However, the Social Studies, History and CCE curriculum are designed to encourage further exploration by both teachers and students.

sentences.speaker: The Acting Minister for Education (Schools) (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: They are provided with references such as the Elections Department website, where they can obtain more information about the process, including ballot secrecy.

sections.label: Students evaluating voting secrecy
sections.summary: By 21, curriculum and exploratory learning with parents equip students to evaluate whether voting is secret.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
sentences.text: Through our curriculum and through the students' own exploratory learning together with their parents, in good time, when they reach 21 years old and beyond, they will be equipped with the necessary skills to evaluate for themselves whether voting is secret.
